_readme: Names/orders for the panchanga engine. Every list below is either 'status': 'standard' (consistent across virtually all sources checked) or 'status': 'needs-sourcing' (genuinely disagrees across texts, or not yet verified against a primary source) — per the project spec, contested items are flagged here rather than silently resolved. 'needs-sourcing' entries still ship a safe generic placeholder (e.g. 'Muhurta 3') so the dial renders correctly while the real names are pending.

location.note: Sringeri, Chikkamagaluru district, Karnataka. Verified against Wikipedia-derived sources and latitude.to.

ayanamsa.note: CONTESTED/APPROXIMATE: Lahiri (Chitrapaksha) ayanamsa is a committee-defined convention, not a closed-form astronomical constant. This engine uses an IAU precession polynomial anchored to the commonly-published J2000 Lahiri value (23°51'25.53"), with a +24.2 arcsec constant calibrated empirically against drikpanchang.com's own published Lahiri Ayanamsha for Sringeri (test/test-harness.html, 11 dates across 2026; sub-arcsecond residual after calibration). This matches drikpanchang's specific Lahiri implementation to high precision but may still differ from other sources (e.g. raw Swiss Ephemeris SE_SIDM_LAHIRI) by a few arcseconds - a calibration choice, not asserted as THE exact Lahiri value. See js/engine/ayanamsa.js.

sunriseDefinition.note: Two valid definitions exist (see js/engine/sunrise.js); this is a user-facing setting, not a disagreement to resolve.

options.upper-limb: Sun's upper limb crosses the horizon, corrected for atmospheric refraction (civil/visual sunrise; matches drikpanchang.com and most almanacs).
options.disc-centre: Geometric centre of the Sun's disc crosses the horizon, no refraction (classical siddhanta-style definition).

ghatiScale.note: CONTESTED, resolved by explicit project-owner decision (not silently): two real conventions exist - fixed-rate (1 ghati = 24 min always, used here) vs day/night-rescaled (sunrise-sunset forced to exactly 30 ghati, which is what drikpanchang.com's own 'Vedic Clock' view uses - confirmed, it shows sunset at exactly '30 Ghati 00 Pala' for Sringeri). Both were implemented and the tradeoff shown directly (under fixed-rate, sunset on an 11h41m day lands at ~29 ghati 12 pala, not a round number; under rescaled it's always exactly 30 by construction); fixed-rate was explicitly chosen. Every ring that places a segment on the dial (muhurta, prahara, kala, Rahu/Yama/Gulika, hora, tithi, nakshatra, day/night) shares this one setting via Ghati.angleForTime, so they're all consistent with each other either way. The rescaled alternative is kept available as VedicEngine.Ghati.currentRescaled. 'pala' vs 'vighati' as the name for 1/60 of a ghati still varies by text; both names are shown.

rescaledAlternative.note: Sunrise-to-sunset and sunset-to-sunrise each forced to exactly 30 ghati; see VedicEngine.Ghati.currentRescaled.

amantaMasa.note: Amanta (South Indian / Karnataka) lunar month names, by sidereal solar rashi (0=Mesha) at the preceding new moon - see js/engine/masa.js. Shown only in the tithi ring's tooltip, since Sringeri itself uses Amanta (not the North Indian Purnimanta convention, which runs about half a month ahead during Krishna Paksha and is not implemented here).

tithi.note: Index 1-15 within each paksha; 15th of shukla = Purnima, 15th of krishna = Amavasya.

nakshatra.note: Some traditions insert 'Abhijit' as an intercalary 28th nakshatra between Uttara Ashadha and Shravana; not included in this 27-nakshatra default list. Flagged, not implemented.

karana.movableSpellingVariant: Some texts spell the 5th movable karana 'Gara' rather than 'Garaja'; drikpanchang.com (cross-checked for Sringeri, 2026) consistently uses 'Garaja', used here.

hora.note: Classical Chaldean descending-speed order. Hora 0 of each Vedic day (starting at sunrise) is ruled by that weekday's own planet; the cycle then runs continuously through day and night (24 horas total: 12 scaled to day length, 12 to night length per js/engine/scaled-intervals.js).

muhurta.note: CONTESTED, resolved to a specific cited primary source rather than a popular-site compilation: names below are Varahamihira's Brihat Samhita (6th c. CE), ch. on muhurtas, as translated by N. Chidambaram Iyer (Madura, South Indian Press, 1884-85; public-domain, hosted at Wellcome Collection and mirrored at wisdomlib.org). A second list is in wide circulation on modern astrology/panchangam sites (day differs at positions 2, 6, 9-13; night is almost entirely different) but is uncredited to any single primary text in every copy found, so it is recorded here as a named variant rather than used as the default. A third, further-differing night sequence appears in Bhagavata-Purana-derived sources and was not fully transcribed. The source also marks the 1st, 2nd, 6th and 7th NIGHT muhurtas (Ishvara, Ajapada, Yama, Vahni) as inauspicious for auspicious undertakings - not yet surfaced in the UI. The 14th night muhurta is Tvashta here (Muhurta Chintamani reportedly agrees: Tvashtra, ruled by Chitra); it is the same span Ayurveda/dharmashastra call Brahma Muhurta (Ashtanga Hridaya Su. 2.1, Arunadatta: 14th muhurta of the night), a time designation rather than a deity name, so per the project owner it is labelled 'Tvaṣṭā (Brahma Muhūrta)'. Display names are in IAST per the project owner; 'Vara' (day 6) and 'Dhala' (night 8) are kept as the 1884 translation spells them, since neither is a clear Sanskrit form (another translation reads the latter as Dhātṛ), so no diacritics were guessed.
muhurta.source: Brihat Samhita of Varahamihira, tr. N. Chidambaram Iyer (1884-85), https://www.wisdomlib.org/hinduism/book/brihat-samhita/d/doc229363.html

contestedVariant.label: Common modern table (uncredited; seen on most popular panchangam/astrology sites)

rashi.note: Sidereal rashi names, 0=Mesha..11=Meena, used for the Lagna ring.

durmuhurta.note: Weekday (0=Sunday..6=Saturday) -> the muhurta(s) that are Durmuhurta, as 0-based indices into the 15-part day (sunrise-sunset) or night (sunset-next sunrise) muhurta division. The standard published rule (as tabulated in Muhurta Chintamani and used by drikpanchang.com): Sun 14th day; Mon 9th and 12th day; Tue 4th day and 7th night; Wed 8th day; Thu 6th and 12th day; Fri 4th and 9th day; Sat 1st and 2nd day. Not yet cross-checked against drikpanchang clock times for Sringeri the way rahuYamaGulika was.

abhijit.note: Abhijit muhurta = the 8th of the 15 day muhurtas (0-based index 7), the one centred on local midday. Not observed on Wednesday, when that same muhurta is the day's Durmuhurta (drikpanchang likewise shows no Abhijit on Wednesdays).

pradosha.note: Pradoṣa kāla: the first 3 of the 15 night muhūrtas (sunset onward, so ~2.5 h, scaled to the night's length). This is the span drikpanchang.com publishes as Pradosh Kaal; some dharmaśāstra texts give only 2 ghaṭī after sunset instead. Shown as good (the Śiva pūjā time).

godhuli.note: Godhūli: half a ghaṭī (12 min) either side of sunset, 24 min in all. Definitions vary (some use a full ghaṭī either side). Shown as good (auspicious for vivāha).

varjyamAmrita.note: Varjyam (tyājya / viṣa ghaṭī, bad) and Amṛta Kālam (amṛta ghaṭī, good): each is a 4-ghaṭī window starting the given number of ghaṭīs after the nakṣatra begins, where 1 ghaṭī = 1/60 of THAT nakṣatra's actual duration (so both scale with how long the nakṣatra lasts). Indexed like nakshatra.names. Varjyam rows 0-22 and 26 confirmed against drikpanchang.com's Nakshatra Thyajyam table (its '51 to 54' = start after 50) and a printed panchang's Thyajya column; Mūla uses 56 (some texts also give 20). Rows 23-25 (Śatabhiṣā 18, P.Bhādrapadā 16, U.Bhādrapadā 24) are the standard values but were not confirmed from a source here. Amṛta: Aśvinī-Rohiṇī, Hasta, Citrā and Revatī confirmed against the Praśnamārga table (wisdomlib); the rest are the commonly used values (as drikpanchang's Amrit Kalam), not yet cross-checked.

prahara.note: Displayed as 'Yaama' per the project owner's preference - 'yama/yaama' is a recognised synonym for this time unit (prahara), researched sources agree it's not individually named in Sanskrit texts beyond being numbered (first-fourth). Distinct from, and not to be confused with, 'Yamaganda/Yama kala' in the rahuYamaGulika scheme below, which is a specific named 1-of-8 segment, not a yaama/prahara - kept as separate internal keys ('prahara' vs 'rahuYamaGulika') specifically to avoid that mixup even though both surface the word 'yama' to the user.

kala.note: Resolved by the user: the five kalas are the classical daytime division Pratah (early morning) - Sangava (forenoon) - Madhyahna (midday) - Aparahna (afternoon) - Sayahna (evening). This scheme is inherently a DAYTIME division (sunrise-to-sunset); no traditional night-time equivalent under these names was identified, so the night half of this ring is left unlabeled rather than inventing five night names.

night.note: No traditional 5-fold night division under this scheme; rendered as a single unlabeled night band.

rahuYamaGulika.note: Weekday -> 0-based segment index within the 8-part DAYTIME (sunrise-to-sunset) division. Empirically derived by cross-checking drikpanchang.com's published Rahu Kalam/Yamaganda/Gulikai Kalam clock times for Sringeri against an 8-way division of that day's actual sunrise-sunset span, for one date per weekday (2026-01-15 Thu, 2026-03-03 Tue, 2026-04-08 Wed, 2026-05-16 Sat, 2026-06-21 Sun, 2026-07-20 Mon, 2026-08-21 Fri) - all 7 weekdays matched a single consistent table, so this is confirmed rather than guessed. CONTESTED/NOT COVERED: night-time Rahu/Yama/Gulika (used in some regional traditions) is not addressed by drikpanchang's daytime table and is left unimplemented here.

nityaYoga.note: Amrita Yogam / Siddha Yogam / Marana Yogam: weekday x nakshatra classification used in Tamil panchangam to mark a nakshatra-span on a given weekday as auspicious (Amrita, most auspicious; Siddha, ordinary-auspicious) or inauspicious (Marana). Every weekday x nakshatra cell is exactly one of the three - transcribed by the project owner from a photographed printed Tamil panchangam table (an 'A/Si/M' = 'அ/சி/ம' grid, column headers the 27 nakshatras, row headers the 7 vaaram), cross-checked by re-reading the photo twice independently (precise per-column crops aligned against the weekday-label column) with full agreement both times. The table carries its own caveat line ('கலிக்காதெனவே கருது', roughly 'considered not to apply in Kali' - a traditional softening disclaimer not to treat these as binding doshas) which is noted here but not otherwise acted on. Marana Yogam here is a DIFFERENT thing from the 27-fold astronomical 'yoga' (Vishkambha..Vaidhriti, sum of sidereal Sun+Moon longitude) already computed by js/engine/yoga.js - same English word, unrelated computation.

legend.S: Siddha Yogam (ordinary auspicious, not separately shown on the dial)

nityaYoga.weekdayIndexOrder: Each row is [Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday], matching VedicEngine.Util.weekdayAtOffset.

sarvarthaSiddhiYoga.note: CONTESTED: weekday x nakshatra combinations treated as universally auspicious ('accomplishes all purposes'). Sources disagree on the exact table and none of those checked cites a primary text (Muhurta Chintamani / Nirnaya Sindhu are claimed by some sites but not quoted). Table below follows hindu-blog.com's list (see source). Spot-checked against drikpanchang.com's own published Sarvartha Siddhi Yoga occurrences for Sringeri-equivalent (New Delhi) timings in October 2026: Monday+Pushya matched (confirmed), but Sunday+Ashwini was shown by drikpanchang (2026-10-25 occurrence, 7:22pm-6:29am) and is NOT in this table's Sunday list - so this table is known to be incomplete/disagreeing with drikpanchang's own (undocumented) rule. Shipped anyway per project convention for contested data (flag rather than silently resolve); revisit if a primary-text table turns up.

raviYoga.note: Formed when the Moon's nakshatra, counted inclusively from the Sun's current (sidereal) nakshatra, lands on the 4th, 6th, 9th, 10th, 13th or 20th position (e.g. Sun in Ashwini -> qualifying Moon nakshatras are Rohini, Ardra, Ashlesha, Magha, Hasta, Purva Ashadha). Not restricted to Sundays despite the name - 'Ravi' refers to using the Sun's nakshatra as the counting origin. Sources agree on this count list (indastro.com, horasarvam.blogspot.com); one source (bhaktibharat.com) gives a conflicting near-inverse list and looks likely to be an error, not used here. Spot-checked against drikpanchang.com's published Ravi Yoga occurrences for New Delhi, October 2026: 2026-10-25 (Sun in Swati, Moon in Revati, count 13) matched exactly.
raviYoga.countNote: Count is 1-based and inclusive of the Sun's own nakshatra, i.e. count = ((moonNakshatraIndex - sunNakshatraIndex + 27) % 27) + 1.

vishaYoga.note: CONTESTED/SINGLE-SOURCE: weekday x tithi (paksha-relative, 1-15) combination treated as inauspicious ('poison yoga'). Only one source found with a concrete rule (a Muhurta Yogas PDF); not cross-checked against a second source or against drikpanchang (no public 'Visha Yoga date finder' found to spot-check against, unlike the other yogas on this dial). Shipped flagged rather than omitted, per project convention for contested/thin data.
